title: One-term Tor-acyclic K-flat tensor comparison
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and B a commutative R-algebra. Let Q be a cochain complex of R-modules supported only in one degree k, meaning Q^n is zero whenever n is not k. Suppose Tor_i^R(Q^k,B)=0 for every positive integer i [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. For every K-flat R-complex P [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] and quasi-isomorphism f:P\to Q, the termwise tensor map f\otimes_R B:P\otimes_R B\to Q\otimes_R B is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Section 15.60, Lemmas 15.60.7, 15.60.9, 15.60.12 and Definition 15.60.13; parent Tag 08IB final affine calculation

proof.text: Convert the support assumption to IsStrictlyGE k and IsStrictlyLE k and use the proved source CochainComplex.isoSingle to identify Q with the single complex on Q.X k. The existing signature, support hypothesis and Tor convention are unchanged.

For M = Q.X k and N = B, take the existing Mathlib projectiveResolution M. In chain degree zero, ChainComplex.quasiIsoAt₀_iff and ShortComplex.quasiIso_iff_of_zeros' reduce the tensor augmentation to exactness and epimorphy of its cokernel map; tensor preserves this cokernel by CokernelCofork.mapIsColimit. In positive chain degrees, ProjectiveResolution.isoLeftDerivedObj identifies homology with the specified Tor' groups [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]; their assumed vanishing gives exactness, and the mapped single complex has zero terms there. Extend along ComplexShape.embeddingUpIntLE k. The proved mapExtendFunctorNatIso and quasiIso_extendMap_iff transport the tensor augmentation calculation to cochain degrees k-i, while extendSingleIso identifies its target with the single complex in degree k.

The extended projective resolution is bounded above by k and has projective, hence flat, terms. Translate flatness using ModuleCat.flat_iff_flat, supply exact integer-indexed colimits using the module AB5 instance and AsSmall.equiv, and apply the closed source CochainComplex.kFlat_of_isStrictlyLE_of_flat. Thus this is a K-flat resolution [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] whose tensor augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism.

Use the proved ModuleCat.hasFunctorialFlatResolution instance and the reduced source LeftResolution.resolutionFunctor T, with natural quasi-isomorphism ρ:T→Id and K-flat values. Naturality and two-out-of-three show T maps quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. The closed generic MorphismProperty.whiskerRight_of_kFlat, transported through map₂HomologicalComplexFlipObjSingleIso, shows termwise tensor with N preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes. For the calculated augmentation g:S→Q, the naturality square for g gives that tensor(ρ_Q) is a quasi-isomorphism, since tensor(T(g)), tensor(ρ_S), and tensor(g) are. The naturality square for the specified f:P→Q then gives that tensor(f) is a quasi-isomorphism, since tensor(T(f)), tensor(ρ_P), and tensor(ρ_Q) are. These squares commute as chain maps; no homotopy refinement or mixed tensor comparison is needed. Transport g through the single-support isomorphism to Q before this comparison.

theorem quasiIso_tensor_of_single_support_tor_acyclic
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
    (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (k : ℤ)
    (hsupport : ∀ n : ℤ, n ≠ k → IsZero (Q.X n))
    (hTor : ∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i →
      IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj (Q.X k)).obj (ModuleCat.of R B)))
    (P : CochainComplex.KFlat (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (f : P.obj ⟶ Q)
    (hf : QuasiIso f) :
    QuasiIso ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R B)).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f)
